about: The LaLonde job-training data: trainees against a general survey sample. re74 and re75 are earnings before training, re78 after. People weren't randomly assigned in this version.
review: Goals and labels drafted by Claude on 2026-11-14, paraphrases written by Claude. Labels reviewed by Ben on 2026-11-18.

goals.goal: Did the job training program raise earnings?
paraphrases: Do people who went through training earn more?
earnings impact of the training
Did training increase income?
did the job trainng raise pay

labels.why: Earnings after training, trainees against similar non-trainees. In this version people weren't randomly assigned, and a plain difference gets the sign wrong (Ben, 2026-11-18).

paraphrases: 1978 earnings, trainees vs non-trainees
Were trainees' 1978 incomes higher?
Is pay in 1978 different for people who trained?
trainees make more in 78?

goals.goal: Was the training worth the money?
goals.note: Worth the money needs the program's cost, which isn't in the table (Ben, 2026-11-18).
paraphrases: Did the training pay off?
Is the program worth funding again?
was training a good investment
Should we keep paying for job training?

goals.goal: Did training help people find work?
paraphrases: Are trainees more likely to be employed afterwards?
employment after training
Did the program get people jobs?
did trainng help ppl get hired

goals.goal: People signed up for training themselves. Are they earning more afterwards?
paraphrases: Trainees self-selected. Is their later income higher?
Not randomized: do people who chose training earn more afterwards?
Among volunteers for training, are later earnings higher?
they picked training themselfs, earning more after?

labels.why: The person flags that trainees chose to train, so they're asking about the effect: later earnings against similar non-trainees (Ben, 2026-11-18).
